strengths: Well-motivated problem diagnosis: Convincingly shows that Prefix-Tuning's failure isn't due to inability to modify attention patterns (Figure 2), but rather an inherent input/prefix significance tradeoff clearly explained via Equation 4

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple datasets, models with different attention mechanisms (MHA/GQA), IID/OOD evaluation with Pareto analysis, varying data sizes, and practical alignment tasks (SFT, DPO, SimPO)
Clear mathematical framework: Progressive development from Equations 5-8 is logical and intuitive; effective decomposition of the attention output with prefixes
Consistent improvements over standard Prefix-Tuning: 29.4% average improvement demonstrates robustness across different settings
Unified framework for context-based methods: Section 5.2 provides useful perspective on design choices in PEFT methods
Good diagnostic analysis: Appendix B includes spectrum analysis, attention visualization, and CKA similarity studies that support the main claims
Well-written and clear presentation: Paper is generally well-structured with compelling motivation
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is relatively incremental—primarily applies linearized attention techniques from [4] with straightforward modifications (fixed convex combination, kernel approximation, trainable matrices). Removing λ and N in practice further reduces elegance of the formulation

Incomplete theoretical understanding: While the paper identifies the tradeoff problem in Equation 4, it lacks rigorous explanation of why moving the prefix outside attention actually solves it. Equation 8 is still attention reweighting, just externalized. The fundamental mathematical constraints aren't analyzed

Arbitrary design choices with insufficient ablation: elu(x) kernel chosen as 'proof of concept' without exploration of alternatives; removing λ justified only by hand-waving about absorption into weights; no ablations comparing kernel approximation vs. exact attention; intermediate design in Eq. 9 never evaluated

Limited evaluation scope: Experiments only on few-shot settings (5-28 examples); models tested are relatively small (3B-7B); primarily classification tasks without generation, reasoning, or code; authors acknowledge no evaluation on abundant data; limited to supervised and alignment settings

Modest and inconsistent empirical improvements over LoRA: Claimed 8.1% average masks inconsistency (24.9% on GoEmotions, 2.9% on DBpedia, 5.6% on BigBench); no error bars or significance testing; results show PT+ is competitive rather than superior to LoRA

Missing critical ablations and sensitivity analysis: No ablation removing kernel approximation; no comparison of keeping prefix in attention head (Eq. 9) vs. external module (Eq. 8); no sensitivity to kernel function; no investigation of M dimensionality; no justification for each architectural removal

Fairness concerns in baseline comparisons: Unclear if hyperparameters equally tuned across methods; LoRA rank set to match parameter count but equivalence not established; no discussion of variance across random seeds; learning rate differences not addressed

Incomplete theoretical grounding: Why does external module M work better than internal biases? Connection between Figure 3 spectrum analysis and downstream performance not established; claims that larger CKA distance equals 'more expressive' are not validated

Narrow scope admits fundamental limitation: Authors acknowledge evaluating only in few-shot settings on small models and similar task types; 'modern LLMs' claims may be overstated; practical relevance for actual modern LLM applications unclear

strengths: Clear and insightful diagnosis of Prefix-Tuning's failure through the prefix-input contribution tradeoff analysis (Eq. 3), with solid empirical verification that PT can modify attention patterns in deep models

Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning diagnostic (few-shot) and large-scale (SFT, DPO, math reasoning) settings with thoughtful IID/OOD generalization analysis via Pareto plots and testing across different attention mechanisms (MHA/GQA)
Substantial empirical improvements on several benchmarks (e.g., 71.2% vs 67.4% on BigBench, 38.6% vs 23.9% improvement on Minerva-Math), with consistent gains on preference alignment tasks
Principled mathematical derivation from Eq. 2→7 clearly motivating design choices, supported by spectrum analysis (Fig. 3) demonstrating increased expressivity of PMT's bias contributions
Efficiency analysis showing competitive throughput and latency, with reasonable parameter efficiency compared to LoRA
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Core contribution is incremental refinement of Chen et al. (2024)—replacing a bias term with trainable matrix M. Kernel approximations are standard; the modification lacks fundamental innovation

Insufficient ablation studies: Critical design choices lack empirical validation—simplifications in Eq. 6→7 (removing λ and φ(qᵢ)ᵀN) justified only informally; limited exploration of feature map choices (only ELU vs GELU); no ablation on M dimensionality

Unjustified mathematical steps: Jump from Eq. 5 (exact sums) to Eq. 6 (trainable M) lacks analysis of approximation quality or information loss. Claim that layer norm 'absorbs' λ needs rigorous justification. ELU kernel choice problematic (negative outputs violate kernel positivity)

Incomplete baseline comparisons: Missing comparisons to recent context-based methods (P-Tuning v2, DePT, ADePT) mentioned in related work; LoRA+ relegated to single table; limits assessment of PMT's position in PEFT landscape

Mixed empirical results with weak statistical rigor: Improvements over LoRA often modest (1-3 points); GoEmotions gains marginal; no significance testing or confidence intervals despite 5-run averaging; some differences likely not statistically significant

Limited experimental scale: Only 3B-7B models tested; claim these are 'proxies for larger architectures' is unvalidated. For 2026 venue standards, 70B+ evaluation expected. Limited evaluation in abundant-data regimes acknowledged in Appendix E

Unclear practical advantage and missing critical analysis: No characterization of when PMT substantially outperforms alternatives; missing empirical case for switching from established LoRA; CKA analysis interpretation unclear (PMT 0.9432 vs LoRA 0.9978 similarity to base)

Reproducibility and design limitation concerns: Code not released; feature map choices artificially constrained (learnable maps dismissed without empirical validation in Remark 1); incomplete justification for design decisions limits future improvements

Overstated claims: '8.1% improvement over LoRA' cherry-picked from few-shot setting; title 'modernizing' Prefix-Tuning suggests broader impact than incremental refinement; 'proof of concept' framing doesn't justify the positioning
